final_lessons: Awaiting feedback on whether high LR helps in low-step budgets.
Adam at moderate LR outperformed high-LR RMSprop; prefer Adam-family optimizers with reasonable LR in low-step budgets.
Adaptive optimizers (Adam/AdamW/RMSprop) with moderate LR reliably beat low-LR SGD/Adagrad under short step budgets.
Adam with moderate-to-high LR on wide models tends to minimize CE fastest in short budgets.
Larger d_model (128) combined with an adaptive optimizer tends to yield the lowest CE.
Among equal-width models, AdamW at moderate LR tends to edge out RMSprop and SGD.
Wide d_model=128 with AdamW at moderate LR consistently produces the lowest CE.
When only one option uses an adaptive optimizer, it typically wins over SGD choices.
Wide d_model=128 plus any adaptive optimizer is the safest bet for lowest CE.
Between two wide adaptive configs, the one with moderate LR beats the one with excessively high LR.
